Subject: FW: initial telemetry — quick triage notes (auth/gateway)

Quick summary of what runtime team sees from initial traces and the logs Jack shared:

- Symptom: broad increase in 5xx and 429 responses across gateway nodes servicing BlueHelm; client traces show aggressive retries after 5xx/429.
- Root candidate: token validation failures (JWT) are being funneled through the gateway auth path, but failing validations are intermittently being classified as 502/503/429 by the front proxy rather than 401.
- Contributing factor: evidence of clock skew on a subset of BlueHelm client hosts -> JWT "nbf/iat/exp" comparisons intermittently fail. That would normally yield a 401, but the gateway path uses an auth cache + rate limiter; when the auth check fails under heavy load the error path collapses to a generic 5xx and triggers upstream rate-limiter responses (429).
- Why retries escalate: BlueHelm's client retry logic treats 5xx/429 as retryable; because upstream was returning those instead of 401, clients pumped more traffic and caused a retry storm.

Immediate mitigations we applied (in the last 30m):
- Isolated BlueHelm traffic to a dedicated routing group to avoid cross-tenant rate limit bleed.
- Bypassed auth-cache layer for BlueHelm while we validate tokens to avoid misclassification.
- Rolled a config that forces strict 401 for 'invalid_token' during validation path on edge for the next 1h.

Next steps (owners):
- Markus/infra: collect and upload full gateway logs and capture tokens (sanitized) -> INFR-5582 (Rishi to own upload).
- Rishi: validate exact clock skew windows from BlueHelm traces and confirm that failing iat/exp matches failure windows.
- Monica: communicate status and ETA back to BlueHelm and coordinate ask for their ops to confirm NTP / clock drift.

I'll be on the bridge in 10.

-Markus

We isolated the problem to two interacting issues: (1) a subset of JWT validations failing due to clock skew on some BlueHelm hosts, and (2) our gateway auth path incorrectly mapping some of those failures to 5xx/429 under high load which induced client retry storms.

Actions we've taken so far:
- Isolated your traffic to a dedicated route and bypassed the auth-cache path to avoid misclassification.
- Deployed a short-term config to ensure token validation failures return 401.
- We collected sanitized logs and a packet capture (attached) for joint analysis.

Subject: Post-incident: BlueHelm outage root cause, mitigations, and next steps

Jack / BlueHelm leadership — final summary from our side after the incident and remediation work:

Root cause: An edge-case combination of (A) short-lived clock skew on a subset of BlueHelm client hosts causing JWT "nbf/iat/exp" failures during a small window (07:28–07:46 PDT on 2027-04-03), and (B) an auth-cache + rate-limiter error path in our gateway that, under load, returned 5xx/429 instead of 401 for token validation failures. The misreported 5xx/429 caused BlueHelm clients to retry aggressively, creating a retry storm and compounding load on the gateway.

What we changed:
- Immediate: isolated tenant routing, bypassed auth-cache, forced 401 on validation failures, rate-limit shields to prevent retry amplification.
- Hotfix: deployed a fix that hardens the error mapping so token validation failures are never returned as 5xx/429; added additional logging to trace auth-code path.
- Longer term: implementing a defensive backoff policy per-tenant, improving auth-cache eviction semantics, and a dashboard to surface auth-error classification anomalies.

Impact: Error rate for BlueHelm peaked at ~18% of requests in the window; estimated customer-facing failures ~22k checkouts affected. We will provide a detailed activity timeline and packet captures in the shared folder.

Compensation: As discussed with Grace, Redwood will apply a 10% credit for April invoice and offer two weeks of elevated support. We will share a formal postmortem doc and invite you to a 1:1 technical review next week.

Owner contacts: Markus Klein (runtime lead), Rishi Malhotra (infra), Monica Patel (AE / primary contact).

Apologies again for the disruption — we take availability seriously and will follow up with the full postmortem and remediation timeline.

- Monica
